topic: The Determinant: The Scaling Factor of Space
target_audience: University students beginning Linear Algebra or advanced High School students

sections.title: The Hook: Meet Leo the Grid-Lion
lecture_lines: Meet Leo, our lion residing on a 2D grid.
Matrices can transform space and change Leo's shape.
Leo's area scales according to the matrix used.
This scaling factor is known as the determinant.
A determinant of six means six times the area.
animations: Introduce a vector-based lion drawing (Leo) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lion.svg] on a light grey grid (#D3D3D3).
Apply a matrix transformation that shears and stretches the grid and Leo.
Fill the original lion's area with translucent blue (#0000FF, 0.4) and the new area with translucent orange (#FFA500, 0.4).
Display text 'Determinant' (#FFFFFF) pointing to the ratio between the orange and blue areas.
Display 'Scale factor: 6' (#FFFF00) as the area comparison is highlighted.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Unit Square and Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: The unit square is defined by basis vectors.
Matrix columns tell us where these vectors land.
This transformation determines the new shape of space.
animations: Display unit vectors i-hat (red, #FF0000) and j-hat (blue, #0000FF) forming a unit square [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg].
Display a 2x2 matrix. Animate i-hat moving to (3,0) and j-hat moving to (0,2) according to the matrix columns.
Show the unit square [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/square.svg] expanding into a 3x2 rectangle, with the grid lines updating to match.

sections.title: Geometric Definition: Area of the Parallelogram
lecture_lines: Transformed basis vectors form a skewed parallelogram.
The determinant measures this parallelogram's area.
For a 2x2 matrix, use the formula ad minus bc.
This number quantifies how much space has stretched.
An area of five means a five-fold expansion.
animations: Transform a unit square into a parallelogram using matrix [[2, 1], [1, 3]].
Fill the parallelogram with a light purple color (#E6E6FA, 0.5) to highlight its area.
Display the formula 'det = (2*3) - (1*1)' in white (#FFFFFF) at the top of the frame.
Highlight the calculation result '5' in bright yellow (#FFFF00) with a pulse effect.
Show five unit-sized squares fitting inside the parallelogram to visually represent the area of 5.

sections.title: Orientation: What if the Determinant is Negative?
lecture_lines: Negative determinants indicate the space has been flipped.
It's like looking at a mirror image of space.
The relative orientation of the basis vectors has reversed.
animations: Show i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#0000FF) swap sides using matrix [[0, 1], [1, 0]].
Briefly show the grid flipping horizontally as if reflected in a mirror [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mirror.svg].
Display 'Determinant = -1' in red (#FF0000) and show a circular arrow indicating the change in orientation.

sections.title: The Critical Case: Determinant Zero
lecture_lines: A zero determinant means space collapses into a line.
Since area is lost, we cannot reverse this transformation.
This is why matrices with zero determinant lack inverses.
animations: Apply matrix [[1, 2], [2, 4]] to the grid, causing all squares to collapse into a single line.
Highlight the collapsed line in red (#FF0000) and show the area shrinking to a line.
Display 'det = 0' and 'No Inverse' in white text (#FFFFFF) next to the collapsed grid.

sections.title: Scaling Up: 3D and Summary
lecture_lines: In 3D, the determinant scales the volume of boxes.
It remains the universal expansion factor for any dimension.
Think of the determinant as the magnitude of stretching.
animations: Show a wireframe cube drawn in perspective. Transform it into a skewed box (parallelepiped) using [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] to represent 3D volume scaling.
Display the word 'Determinant' (#FFD700) and show it linking to terms: '2D: Area', '3D: Volume'.
The transformed box [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/box.svg] flashes in bright yellow (#FFFF00) as the value 'Volume = det(A)' appears.
